title: indigo_mount_lx200: MOUNT_STATE slew light does not follow a kept coordinates ALERT; a GoTo handled before the first poll is published OK
description: Audit in 1078b2c4 found the same order defect as in synscan (the light is computed before indigo_update_coordinates()). Second part, approved by the owner for this ticket: on the profiles decoded by meade_update_generic_state() a GoTo handled before the first poll of a session (or after a sync whose readback failed) is published OK by that poll while the mount is still slewing, because last_position_valid is false and there is nothing to compare with (review remark of 82634c3e). Fix by seeding lastRA/lastDec from a position read in meade_init_mount() (one extra round trip at connect) and after a failed sync readback as far as possible, with a simulator case. Owner's rule (decided 2026-11-22 for mount_synscan, ticket 1078b2c4, and extended to this driver on 2026-11-23): whenever MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES is in ALERT, the SLEW light of MOUNT_STATE is ALERT too; BUSY while the coordinates are BUSY; otherwise as before. The library keeps a coordinates ALERT until the next BUSY (indigo_update_coordinates() kept-ALERT rule, indigo_reject_coordinates_change()), so the light must be derived from the coordinates state after indigo_update_coordinates() has decided it, at every place the driver publishes the coordinates or MOUNT_STATE (poll, refusals, sync, abort, park/home, connect), not from the driver's own motion flags alone. Reference implementation: synscan_update_mount_state() and its call order in indigo_drivers/mount_synscan/indigo_mount_synscan.driver (commit 5f794cc15). Scope: the .driver source (version bump, regenerate with the unchanged generator), simulator-backed cases proving the light follows the coordinates state through a refused/failed request (ALERT kept while idle), the next accepted request (BUSY, then OK/IDLE) and connect, adaptation of existing cases that asserted IDLE under a kept ALERT, recorded run with tools/run_driver_test.py, MIGRATION_STATUS count. Refusals inserted by the generator (parked/homing guards) cannot call driver code; if the light lags there until the next poll, record it in the ticket note and do not change the generator.

outcome.summary: Part 1 (slew light) correct. Required: indigo_mount_lx200.driver:3526-3533 meade_seed_last_position() sets lastRA/lastDec and last_position_valid but leaves positionRA/positionDec stale (0 or the previous session); the poll copies positionRA into lastRA even when its readback failed (3802-3803), so 'seed OK, first poll read fails' makes the next good poll report a false slew (reproduced: head 1 BUSY, master 0). Fix: also set positionRA/positionDec in the seed; add a simulator case (seed OK, first poll readback fails, no BUSY over the following polls); repeat the recorded run. Non-blocking: after a sync handled while a poll lit BUSY the light stays BUSY under OK until the next poll (set IDLE in the sync success branch when not slewing - optional); poll publishing ALERT during a pending sync leaves the light IDLE until the next poll; AP with :GOS# whose status read fails falls back to position decoding without a seed; first variant of the goto-before-first-poll case does not tell connect seed from handler seed; classic-guiding refusal light untested.

Round 2 (head f813f64db): meade_seed_last_position() now sets positionRA/positionDec with lastRA/lastDec; new case lx200_generic_first_poll_readback_fails_after_the_connect_read passes on head and fails on the round-one driver (reviewer ran both); the sync-branch IDLE cannot switch off the light during real motion (slewing is the last poll's verdict on the same queue; a real slew makes the sync refused); generated files byte-identical; MIGRATION count 180 = 177 + 3 TCP, other rows as on master. Non-blocking: sync-branch IDLE has no dedicated case (timing-dependent window) and is published before the readback and the coordinates' OK; connect seed vs handler seed not covered separately.

history.text: Editing the .driver: slew light after coordinates, position seed at connect
Writing simulator cases: slew light follows coordinates, goto before first poll
Running filtered lx200 cases: new slew light and goto-before-first-poll cases
Running adapted lx200 cases filtered, and the new cases against the pre-change driver
Recorded run failed in sync_result (3 generic-decoded profiles): seed no longer writes published coordinates; rerunning

Implementation (indigo_mount_lx200 version 89 -> 90, .driver edited, .c regenerated with the unchanged generator; the generated diff equals the .driver diff apart from indentation and DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000059 -> 0x0300005A; .h and _main.c unchanged).

Cause 1 (slew light): the poll published MOUNT_STATE before indigo_update_coordinates(), with the light its own branches chose (IDLE on the "read OK" branch, BUSY while decelerating after an abort), so under a coordinates ALERT kept by the library the light was IDLE/BUSY; the slew-failed, sync-failed and classic-guiding refusal paths never touched the light; the abort set it IDLE; a new session kept whatever light the last one ended with.
Fix 1: one profile-independent helper meade_update_slew_light(): coordinates ALERT -> light ALERT, BUSY -> BUSY, otherwise the caller's light, except that an ALERT light never outlives the coordinates ALERT (-> IDLE). Called (a) in the poll after indigo_update_coordinates(), MOUNT_STATE now published after the coordinates (still once per poll, as before); (b) in the abort handler after the "Goto aborted" ALERT; (c) after the classic-guiding indigo_reject_coordinates_change(); (d) at the end of the MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES on_change, before the generated indigo_update_coordinates(): the macro INDIGO_COPY_TARGETS_PROCESS_COORDINATES_CHANGE published the request BUSY just before, so the result state is published unchanged (MOUNT_STATE published only when the light changed); (e) meade_init_mount() sets the light IDLE and derives it from the coordinates (OK at session start). The 8 places that assign MOUNT_STATE_SLEW_ITEM keep their values; the helper overrides them.
Consequence: a poll that runs between the BUSY of a request and its handler now lights BUSY (coordinates BUSY) instead of waiting for the handler after :MS#; for a sync request in that window the light flashes BUSY for one poll.
Not covered: refusals inserted by the generator (parked guard "Mount is parked!") cannot call
Implementation resumed: the review requested changes
Addressing review: seed sets positionRA/Dec, new seed-then-failed-poll case, sync light, merge master
Recorded run after review fixes: python3 tools/run_driver_test.py mount_lx200

Review round 1 (changes) addressed. Defect: meade_seed_last_position() set lastRA/lastDec and last_position_valid but left positionRA/positionDec stale (0 on a first connect, the previous session's last read otherwise); a poll whose readback fails copies positionRA/Dec into lastRA/Dec, so 'seed OK, first poll readback fails' made the next successful poll report a false slew (1 BUSY coordinates + 1 BUSY light). Fix: the seed sets positionRA/positionDec too (positionRA = lastRA = ra, positionDec = lastDec = dec); the goto handler uses the same function, so it is consistent. New case lx200_generic_first_poll_readback_fails_after_the_connect_read: generic profile, a fault on the next :GR# is armed from the log line of the seed's :GD#, so the first poll's readback fails (asserted 'fault GR'); over 3 complete polls no BUSY coordinates and no BUSY slew light, coordinates OK and light IDLE at the end. Without the fix line (generated .c with only the positionRA/positionDec assignments reverted, linked into the same test): 'after the failed readback: 1 BUSY coordinates, 1 BUSY slew lights', FAIL expected 0, got 1; with it PASS. Extra (a): in the sync success branch the light is set IDLE and MOUNT_STATE published when it was BUSY and the last poll saw no slew (a BUSY lit by a poll between the sync's admission and its handler no longer stays under OK until the next poll); no dedicated case (the window is timing-dependent), covered only by the existing sync cases. Extra (b) skipped: telling the connect seed from the handler seed in lx200_generic_goto_before_the_first_poll needs a new events-between helper (counting :GR#/:GD# between connect and :Sr#), more than a few lines; the read-fails variant already proves the handler seed by the asserted single 'fault GR'. Merged master (git merge, 5fbf21d11): conflict only in MIGRATION_STATUS.md, resolved with master's mount_ioptron 147 and lx200 180; TEST_SUMMARY auto-merged. notes.text:
Implementation (indigo_mount_lx200 version 89 -> 90, .driver edited, .c regenerated with the unchanged generator; the generated diff equals the .driver diff apart from indentation and DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000059 -> 0x0300005A; .h and _main.c unchanged).

Cause 1 (slew light): the poll published MOUNT_STATE before indigo_update_coordinates(), with the light its own branches chose (IDLE on the "read OK" branch, BUSY while decelerating after an abort), so under a coordinates ALERT kept by the library the light was IDLE/BUSY; the slew-failed, sync-failed and classic-guiding refusal paths never touched the light; the abort set it IDLE; a new session kept whatever light the last one ended with.
Fix 1: one profile-independent helper meade_update_slew_light(): coordinates ALERT -> light ALERT, BUSY -> BUSY, otherwise the caller's light, except that an ALERT light never outlives the coordinates ALERT (-> IDLE). Called (a) in the poll after indigo_update_coordinates(), MOUNT_STATE now published after the coordinates (still once per poll, as before); (b) in the abort handler after the "Goto aborted" ALERT; (c) after the classic-guiding indigo_reject_coordinates_change(); (d) at the end of the MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES on_change, before the generated indigo_update_coordinates(): the macro INDIGO_COPY_TARGETS_PROCESS_COORDINATES_CHANGE published the request BUSY just before, so the result state is published unchanged (MOUNT_STATE published only when the light changed); (e) meade_init_mount() sets the light IDLE and derives it from the coordinates (OK at session start). The 8 places that assign MOUNT_STATE_SLEW_ITEM keep their values; the helper overrides them.
Consequence: a poll that runs between the BUSY of a request and its handler now lights BUSY (coordinates BUSY) instead of waiting for the handler after :MS#; for a sync request in that window the light flashes BUSY for one poll.
Not covered: refusals inserted by the generator (parked guard "Mount is parked!") cannot call driver code; the light lags there until the next poll (<= 1 s), which then derives it. Edge: if a poll publishes ALERT (readback failures beyond retries or a Gemini stall) between the BUSY of a sync request and its handler, the OK of the sync is kept as ALERT by the library while the handler derives IDLE from OK; the next poll corrects the light.

Cause 2 (goto before the first poll): profiles decoded by meade_update_generic_state() (generic, classic, StarGO2, AP without :GOS#) had last_position_valid false until the first poll, so a goto handled before it was published OK by that poll while the mount slewed.
Fix 2: meade_seed_last_position() reads the controller position with meade_get_coordinates() (controller frame, like positionRA/positionDec) into lastRA/lastDec; it does not touch the published coordinates (a first attempt with meade_read_position() wrote them before the properties were defined, so the first poll published no fresh OK and lx200_sync_result_carries_the_reported_position failed for generic, classic and stargo2 in the first recorded run; fixed, see below). Called at the end of meade_init_mount() for those profiles only (one extra :GR#/:GD# round trip at connect, appended after the site read; other profiles' connect traces unchanged); a failed read leaves last_position_valid false as before (no false slew). Failed sync readback path: the goto handler (TRACK branch) of those profiles reads the start position the same way when last_position_valid is false, before :Sr#/:Sd#/:MS#; this also covers a failed read at connect. Remains: if that read fails too, the first poll after the goto still has nothing to compare with and publishes the goto OK; a goto started from the hand controller right after such a sync is seen one poll late, as before. No position is invented.

Tests (indigo_test/integration/test_mount_lx200_simulator.c):
- New lx200_slew_light_follows_kept_coordinates_alert (generic = position-decoded, ZWO = native status): after connect OK/IDLE over a poll (c); :MS# refused by fault rule -> coordinates ALERT and light ALERT at once and after each of 2 complete polls of the idle mount (a); next goto -> BUSY light published, ends OK at target, light IDLE over 2 polls (b); a second refusal, disconnect, reconnect -> coordinates OK and light IDLE at definition and over 2 polls (c).
- New lx200_generic_goto_before_the_first_poll: the client sends the goto from its own update callback when CONNECTION is published OK (queued ahead of the first poll); the coordinates must be published OK only at the target (RA 18, DEC -80), with >= 2 BUSY coordinate publications and a BUSY light, then OK/IDLE over 2 polls. Second variant: a fault rule written from the log line of :Gg# makes the connect seed read fail (asserted: exactly 1 "fault GR"), the goto handler's own read covers it.
- Adapted: lx200_goto_abort_ends_alert_and_idle_abort_keeps_state (light ALERT after the abort and over the polls that keep the ALERT, waited for since MOUNT_STATE follows the coordinates; slew_light_precedes_the_next_poll() now requires the BUSY light before the first poll after :MS#, no longer after :MS#, because a poll between request and handler lights it with the coordinates BUSY; the IDLE light at the end of the next goto is taken from the MOUNT_STATE published after the coordinates' OK); lx200_goto_abort_keeps_alert_while_decelerating (light ALERT instead of BUSY while decelerating and instead of IDLE after the axes stood; IDLE after the next goto).
- Proof without the fix: both new cases built against the pre-change driver object (master's indigo_mount_lx200.c) fail: slew light case "expected 3, got 0" (ALERT expected, IDLE published) for generic and zwo; goto case "goto ended OK at RA 8.8183 DEC 16.9261 after 1 BUSY coordinates", coordinates_at(18, -80) failed, and the read-fails variant failed.
- Filtered runs with the fix: the 4 *_no_slew_without_motion cases, lx200_zwo_park_and_home_requests_during_poll, lx200_sync_result_carries_the_reported_position, classic guiding refusal, failed readback, busy overlap, generic polling progress, disconnect/reconnect: all PASS.
- Recorded run: python3 tools/run_driver_test.py mount_lx200 -> "2026-11-23 16:18 3.0.0.90 mac arm64 simulator 176/176 OK" (first recorded run 176/175 Failed on the seed writing the published coordinates, fixed, record replaced). MIGRATION_STATUS mount_lx200: 177 -> 179 (176 script-run cases + 3 opt-in TCP cases). flow check (whitespace) passed.
Scenario mapping: (a) refused goto ALERT kept over polls -> slew_light_follows_kept (generic, zwo) and goto_abort_ends (onstep, abort path) and goto_abort_keeps_alert_while_decelerating (all status dialects); (b) next request BUSY then OK/IDLE -> same three; (c) connect -> slew_light_follows_kept (connect and reconnect after a kept ALERT); goto before first poll -> generic_goto_before_the_first_poll; settled_state untouched.
Not verified: Linux, Windows, hardware (no hardware run), the opt-in TCP cases (not run by the script), the classic-guiding refusal light (path changed, only the existing case without light assertion ran).
